reasoning: The core problem — detecting from activation statistics when a forward pass has been maliciously steered, with a detection-vs-magnitude tradeoff and false-positive control on clean inputs — is largely addressed by "Steering Awareness: Detecting Activation Steering from Within" (arXiv 2511.21399, Nov 2025). That paper derives the optimal external statistical detector as a matched-filter on activation statistics (s = v^T Σ⁻¹(H'−μ(x))), empirically confirms a sharp detection-vs-steering-magnitude transition (0% at α=0.5 to 94% at α=2), shows direction-dependence, and reports zero false positives on clean controls — covering the proposal's framing including malicious 'comply with harmful request'-type directions and the FPR concern. The main remaining gap is methodological: that paper's empirical detector is fine-tuned introspection from within the model, whereas the proposal trains an external lightweight one-class/logistic detector on simple per-layer stats and reports an AUROC-vs-magnitude curve; this is the natural empirical instantiation of their already-published theory rather than a novel question. Adjacent activation-based tampering/OOD monitors (HuggingFace universal monitor, SafetyNet) and the broad activation-anomaly-detection literature further reduce novelty.

evidence.title: Steering Awareness: Detecting Activation Steering from Within
evidence.summary: Directly addresses detecting injected steering vectors. Derives the optimal external statistical detector as a matched-filter on activation statistics (s = v^T Σ⁻¹(H'−μ(x))), and empirically shows a sharp detection-vs-magnitude transition (0% at α=0.5 to 94% at α=2), strong direction-dependence (r>0.9 with training vector cosine), and zero false positives on clean controls. Empirical detector is fine-tuned in-model introspection (95.5% on held-out concepts) rather than an external lightweight stats classifier, but the theory section establishes the proposal's exact statistical-detection framing and predictions.

evidence.title: Steering Awareness: Models Can Be Trained to Detect Activation Steering
evidence.summary: Community write-up of the above paper. Notes detection generalizes across extraction methods and that detectability is governed by cosine alignment of the steering direction with logistic/SVM/centroid directions vs orthogonal PCA/ICA components, directly relevant to the proposal's clean-vs-steered detection question and magnitude/direction tradeoffs.

evidence.title: Universal activation-based monitor for LLM weight tampering & OOD detection (6 models validated)
evidence.summary: An activation-based monitor explicitly built to flag tampering (weight tampering) and out-of-distribution forward passes from internal activations, validated across several open models. Adjacent realization of the proposal's external activation-statistics monitor, though framed around weight tampering/OOD rather than steering-vector injection specifically.

evidence.title: SafetyNet: Detecting Harmful Outputs in LLMs by Probing Internal States
evidence.summary: Monitoring framework that analyzes a model's internal activations to flag harmful/anomalous behavior, exploiting that later layers capture task-relevant features. Demonstrates the lightweight-internal-state-monitor approach the proposal targets, in an adjacent harmful-output-detection setting.

evidence.title: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection for Quirky Language Models
evidence.summary: Trains anomaly detectors (e.g., Mahalanobis/activation-distance based) on clean activations to flag anomalous behavior, reporting AUROC. Provides the exact detector family (distance-from-clean-distribution, AUROC evaluation) the proposal would use, in an adjacent (quirky-behavior) rather than malicious-steering setting.
